title: fix(cli): hand the data engine the host crypto provider at kernel:ready, before the webhook dispatcher arms
body:
<!-- claude-projects-attribution: {"github_login":"os-elon-musk"} -->
_Requested by **Elon** · [project thread](https://claude.ai/code/project/chan_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9D?thread=cmsg_01WedDzV26nniwxv7jC88B9DDZYUbJbnXUTqZoZ56k4czR)_
Fixes #33342

Clause-②: yes (widening)
Metadata-protocol: none

## 维护者速读

- **改了什么**:`os serve` 在宿主加密插件的 `kernel:ready` 钩子里选定加密提供者的同一刻,就把它交给数据引擎;原来要等 `runtime.start()` 返回后才交。
- **为什么改**:webhook 分发器在更晚的 `kernel:ready` 钩子里启动并解密签名密钥,所以每次启动都会先把带签名的 webhook 停放(报 ERROR),启动窗口内(种子数据、端口已开后的请求)命中的事件被记成永不可重投的死投递,原因只是启动顺序。
- **风险与回滚**:风险低,只把交接时刻提前到「选定提供者」那一刻,失败即关闭(fail-closed)不变:不发未签名请求、不落明文;回滚即 revert 本 PR。
- **先看**:`packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts` 的 `createHostCryptoProvider`(钩子内交接 + `wiredEngine()`)、同文件启动后的确认块(只给钩子没交到的引擎补交)、`serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts` 新增的启动顺序用例。
- **两分钟验证**:`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --project integration src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts`,预期 38 个全过;把钩子里的 `engine.setCryptoProvider(provider);` 删掉再跑,启动顺序用例转红(签名密钥为 undefined,事件被停放)。
- **需要你做的**:无,席位落地。

## What changes

`os serve` composes ONE crypto provider (`createHostCryptoProvider`): its plugin chooses the provider in its own `kernel:ready` hook, and the datasource binder and the settings service already held it from there. The data engine, which backs `secret` fields, was handed it only after `runtime.start()` returned.

The webhook dispatcher (plugin-webhooks) arms in a later `kernel:ready` hook and decrypts every subscription's signing secret on its first cache build. So on every boot of a deployment with a signed `sys_webhook` row:

- the first build failed closed and PARKED the subscription, logging `error` ("holds an encrypted signing secret that could not be decrypted");
- every matching record change until the hand-over (an app seed at `kernel:bootstrapped`, a request once `kernel:listening` opened the port) was recorded as a `dead` `sys_http_delivery` row with 0 attempts and no signature, never sent and never redeliverable — refused for boot order alone;
- the subscription re-armed only when the post-start `setCryptoProvider` fired the engine's `onCryptoProviderChange` listener.

**The fix:** the host plugin's `kernel:ready` hook now hands the data engine the provider at the moment it chooses it (`secretFieldEngineOf`: the `data` service, else `objectql`, feature-detected on `setCryptoProvider`, the same lookup the post-start block makes). The post-start block still runs `confirm()` (a provider registered after init, or replaced, still refuses the boot) and hands the provider only to an engine that hook did not reach (`wiredEngine()`). `run()` mounts the host plugin before the capability resolver that mounts plugin-webhooks, and kernel:ready hooks run in init order, so the hand-over lands before the dispatcher arms.

**Why this fix and not holding early deliveries in the dispatcher:** it is the smaller correct fix, and it removes the cause rather than buffering its effect. The provider is already chosen at that moment and the binder and settings service already use it, so the engine joining them changes no choice. Holding deliveries would need an in-memory queue in the enqueuer with a deadline for a provider that never arrives and a refusal path at that deadline — new state on the hot path, and a queue that a crash loses — to work around a hand-over that was simply late.

**Red lines kept:** nothing is ever sent unsigned and nothing falls back to plaintext. A boot with no usable provider fails closed exactly as before (a production boot without a stable key still stops at `kernel:ready`, before anything is handed). No delivery is held, so none can be dropped: an event is delivered signed, or, for a credential that really cannot be opened, recorded as the same dead row as before.

| During boot, from the host plugin's `kernel:ready` hook until `runtime.start()` returns | FROM | TO |
|:---|:---|:---|
| Dispatcher's first cache build, `sys_webhook` row with a signing secret | `error` + subscription PARKED until the post-start hand-over | secret opens; no `error`, nothing parked |
| A record change matching it (seed at `kernel:bootstrapped`, request after `kernel:listening`) | `dead` delivery, 0 attempts, unsigned, never redeliverable | ordinary delivery, HMAC-signed |
| A `secret` field written or resolved through the data engine | refused, "no CryptoProvider is registered" (fail-closed) | sealed or opened by the provider the boot chose |

## Tests

New top-level `describe` in the shared harness `packages/cli/src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts` (the boot-order pin): a REAL `ObjectKernel`, a REAL `ObjectQL` engine with no provider (as serve's starts), a `sys_webhook` row whose signing secret a previous boot sealed under the local key, the host plugin, and a REAL `AutoEnqueuer` armed from a later plugin's `kernel:ready` hook (the capability resolver's position). A record event fired at `kernel:bootstrapped` (an app seed) must be enqueued with the signing secret and no `undeliverableReason`, with no `error` logged, and `wiredEngine()` must name the engine. Two source pins in `the wiring inside run()` move with the shape: both hand-overs, exactly two `.setCryptoProvider(` call sites, and the host plugin mounted before the capability resolver.

`pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli exec vitest run --maxWorkers=2 --project integration src/commands/serve-host-crypto-provider.test.ts` → `Test Files 1 passed (1)`, `Tests 38 passed (38)`, lock `VERDICT command-exit 0`.
</details>

<details><summary>Ablation (one-shot, not kept): the pin goes red without the hand-over</summary>

`node scripts/ablation-replace.mjs --file packages/cli/src/commands/serve.ts --anchor 'engine.setCryptoProvider(provider);' --replacement 'void provider; /* ABLATED-33342 */'` → anchor x1 → x0, blob `675bda9008` → `67bb30be86` (mutation landed). The pin: `FAIL … an event fired at kernel:bootstrapped (an app seed) is enqueued SIGNED, never parked for boot order` — `AssertionError: expected undefined to be 'whsec_boot_order'` (the delivery reached the enqueue as a parked one, unsigned). Restored: blob == HEAD (`675bda9008`), `git diff HEAD` empty. The test imports `./serve.js` relatively (source, no `dist/` in the path), so no rebuild leg is owed.
</details>

Full `@objectstack/cli` suite (unit + integration, because `serve.ts` is a boot path), after `pnpm --filter @objectstack/cli build`, under the verify lock:

- integration: 21/21 files, 109/109 tests;

An earlier run on a closure-only build failed 23 files, all with "packages/cli is not built" (the dist spawn pins), which the rebuilt run cleared. ## Acceptance notes

- **Measured premise (trace on `origin/main` at `19cc8976bf`):** `serve.ts` handed the engine its provider after `await runtime.start()` (the post-start block), while the host plugin chose it in its `kernel:ready` hook; `WebhookOutboxPlugin` arms `AutoEnqueuer.start()` from its own `kernel:ready` hook, whose first `refresh()` calls `resolveSecretField`; the kernel runs `kernel:ready`, then `kernel:bootstrapped` (`AppPlugin` inline seeds), then `kernel:listening` (the port opens), all inside `runtime.start()`. The ablation leg below is that `main` shape and reproduces the park.
- **Residual, not changed here:** a stack that mounts `WebhookOutboxPlugin` explicitly in its own `plugins[]` (none in this repo; the capability resolver is the only mount) inits before the host plugin, so its dispatcher still arms first and relies on the existing `onCryptoProviderChange` re-arm, as today. Hosts other than `os serve` that wire their own engine after start (`packages/verify/src/harness.ts`, and any host in `objectstack-ai/cloud`) keep their own order. carrier: cloud — noted, not filed.
- **Residual, an app-composed webhooks plugin (review#3 boundary flag 1):** a `plugin-webhooks` that an app lists in its own stack `plugins` is mounted in the stack loop, which runs before the host crypto plugin is mounted. Its `kernel:ready` hook therefore runs first and still parks, and it recovers through the existing re-arm after start, as before this PR.
- **Residual, a late registration inside the new window (review#3 boundary flag 2):** `confirm()` (which refuses a provider registered after init, or replaced) still runs only after start. A boot that `confirm()` will refuse can now seal `secret` writes during the window under the provider `resolve()` chose first, where before the window refused them. That boot is still refused. The case needs a misbehaving plugin and a boot that stops.
- The docblocks of `onCryptoProviderChange` (objectql `engine.ts`, plugin-webhooks `webhook-secret.ts`) and `AutoEnqueuer.start()` still describe the post-start hand-over as the rule; the re-arm channel stays correct as the fallback for the residual above. Left untouched to keep this diff disjoint from the open E2 work in plugin-webhooks.
- The overlapping E2 branch (`claude/area-E2-33263`, PR 33450) changes one line in `auto-enqueuer.ts` (`resolveDeclared`); this diff touches no plugin-webhooks file.
